summary: Dashboard annotation buffer overwrite causes alerts to show wrong trace context
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that alerts triggered by a saved dashboard time-range show trace links and alert context that point to a different time window and unrelated tracehook IDs. The root cause appears tied to the dashboard annotation buffer being overwritten when background annotation compaction runs during retention pruning.

Impact: Multiple alert notifications sent to the customer's PagerDuty and Slack had trace links that, when clicked, opened traces from a different time window. This caused investigation delays and two false escalations. Affects scheduled and ad-hoc alerts for the last 72 hours for the customer's org.

Expected behavior: Alert notifications should include tracehook link(s) that correspond to the exact span/time-window that produced the alert evaluation. Saved dashboards edits and retention compaction should not mutate annotation/tracehook linkage for past alert events.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has a saved dashboard with an annotation query that attaches a tracehook header to series (tracehook: org-clipboard:env-prod).
2) Configure a scheduled alert on a panel with a 5m evaluation window and a notification channel (Slack + PagerDuty).
3) Wait for background retention compaction to run (nightly window) or trigger retention prune on a test dataset.
4) Save a minor edit to the dashboard (change description only) while compaction is in-flight.
5) Observe the next alert notification; click the trace link from the alert and note the time window/trace ID mismatches (points to older/other traces).
investigation: Initial triage: Support reproduced wrong trace links in staging by replaying saved-dashboard edit + compaction in a tight loop. The tracehook token in alert payloads was observed to be replaced with a buffer slot from the compaction batch occasionally.

Hypothesis: Annotation buffer is using shared slot sequencing without sufficient copy-on-write protection when a saved-view edit (metadata change) persists annotations concurrently with compaction eviction. This leads to annotation->tracehook mapping pointing at the wrong buffer index for subsequent alert payload serializations.

Data: We found compactor logs showing 'buffer_overwrite_detected=true' matching times of saved-view commits for the org. Alerting code serializes tracehook references to the current buffer index; when compaction moves entries, the index can be reallocated, causing stale link resonance.
Temporary mitigation attempted: Added a queueing delay in alert worker to re-resolve tracehook by absolute trace_id when available. Reduced but did not eliminate mismatches in test replays.
Repro rate in staging: ~3/10 when compaction and dashboard save overlap within 60s window. In prod customer trace, observed 2 wrong links across 7 alerts in a 24h period.
Related: COMP-332 (annotation compactor refactor) has recent commit that changed buffer allocation semantics; candidate for regression source. See PR github.com/redwood/compactor/pull/1122
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer submitted with screenshots of Slack message and trace link that opened an unrelated trace. Marking P1 because PagerDuty was triggered twice.
2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz (Oncall SRE): Able to reproduce in staging. Added compaction logs and flagged buffer_overwrite. Assigning to infra eng to validate allocator semantics.

2026-03-11 - Priya Menon (Infra Eng): Reproduced locally, bisected to compactor PR 1122. We see buffer slots being reused before alert serialization completes. Planning hotfix to enforce slot immutability for active references.
2026-03-11 - Customer (ClipBoard Analytics): Thanks—this is causing confusion for our oncall. Do you have ETA for a fix?

2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Hotfix branch created (github.com/redwood/compactor/commit/ae45bf2). Will roll to canary in us-east tomorrow 03/13, then to prod 03/14 if green. Notifying customer of planned maintenance window.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Added follow-up task INT-90021 to add unit test coverage for concurrent saved-view edits + compaction; will track separately.
resolution: Workaround: For affected orgs we enabled re-resolve-by-trace-id in the alert worker to reduce incorrect links. Hotfix deployed to compactor which enforces copy-on-write for annotation buffer slots referenced by active alert serializations. Canary rollout started 2026-03-13 in us-east; prod rollout targeted 2026-03-14 after monitoring shows no regression. Postmortem and a follow-up internal ticket (INT-90021) created to harden tests and add observability metrics for buffer reuse. Customer notified and offered 1:1 postmortem review.
